b52QrT6VFVQM.text: Let's consider how ternary logic could represent different values

yRZ2dYkpQTj4.text: Since each flit can be one of three values, the total number of possible combinations can be calculated by raising 3 to the power of the number of flits

TvFfRp4x7AGL.text: We need to find the smallest number of flits to represent at least 256 different values

M8uYGEh8rn6F.text: Since 3^4 = 81 (which is less than 256), 3^5 = 243 (which is less than 256) but 3^5 + 3^4 is also less than 256

2xx6qGcpXRbb.text: 3^6 = 729 (which is greater than 256, but 3^5 + 3^1 = 243 + 3 = 246 which is less than 256), thus the least additional value when having 6 flits would be greater than 256

3iaqE24U7ZpH.text: However in our case we have to find the minimum number of flits to represent 256 or more values (minimum value can be included)

sbfpzYwQMh5j.text: 3^3 is not less than 256 but 7th ternary number would be greater than 256 (3^1 is not included as it would just be "true"), so lets break it down
